Subject: Request — expanded trial credits for Nimbus Labs

Hi Mina,

Thanks for taking my call earlier. Quick follow up — we’re kicking off an exploratory evaluation across four product teams at Nimbus (Search, Recommendations, Analytics, and Internal Tools). The teams will each need roughly 200k tokens/mo for 6 weeks to validate latency and cost assumptions.

We signed up under separate trial accounts to segment access but would like to consolidate or be approved for a one-time expansion of free credits across our org to make the evaluation meaningful. Can Redwood approve a stacked trial credit for Nimbus Labs (company domain nimbuslabs.com)?

Attached is a short Q2 forecast and the list of the trial accounts we created. We’re on a tight timeline — would appreciate a quick decision.

Thanks,
Alex Hart
Head of ML, Nimbus Labs
alex.hart@nimbuslabs.com

Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 2 Apr 2027 10:05:00 -07:00

Hi Alex —

Appreciate the context and the forecast. I’ve looped in Ben (Sales Ops) to review the commercial side and Ben, I’m flagging this to the fraud/compliance triage if the request spans multiple trial accounts.

A few quick asks to help speed the review:
- Can you confirm the list of sign-up emails (or HubSpot account) for the four teams?
- Are the four accounts under a single legal entity / billing domain?
- Any previous trial extensions or separate top-ups we should know about?

Policy note: we do not generally grant cross-account credit stacking without a short due-diligence review — especially when accounts were created independently. If you can send the sign-up emails and company registration link, we can expedite.

Best,
Mina Haddad

Priyom — forwarding a credit expansion request from Nimbus Labs (DB-83421). Mina looped me in.

Why I’m escalating: Nimbus spun up multiple trial accounts under similar company name but different emails; they asked for a consolidated credit allocation. Before we sign off commercially, can you run a quick fraud pattern check? Specifically:
- Were the accounts created from the same IP ranges or VPNs?
- Any history of rapid sequential trial use / multiple top-ups?
- Are the billing/emails obviously related (aliases, plus-addresses, etc.)?

I attached a dump of their trial IDs and basic sign-up metadata. If it’s clean, we can approve a one-time credit grant (recommended: 400k tokens org-level for 6 weeks) and route the rest through a short pilot contract. If it looks suspect, we’ll offer an immediate paid pilot discount instead and deny stacking.

Thanks — Ben
Ben Carter
Sales Operations Manager
Attachment: trial_history.csv
From: Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 3 Apr 2027 09:12:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Nimbus Labs — request for expanded trial credits across teams

Ben / Mina —

I ran the triage against our logs and here are the highlights:
- Signups: four accounts created over 72 hours from overlapping IP subnets (same /24) and identical browser fingerprint markers in the signup payloads.
- Auth & Billing: two accounts used company emails at nimbuslabs.com; two used personal gmail addresses with similar local-parts (alex.hart+team1@gmail.com, alex.hart+team2@gmail.com).
- Prior activity: one of the emails shows a prior trial top-up 9 months ago (manual credit extension).
- Token patterns: initial experiments drove heavy embedding calls then short bursts of generation; usage cadence matches scripted test harnesses rather than organic product use.

Conclusion / recommendation: pattern looks inconsistent with four independent teams testing at separate customers. Likely coordinated single-organization evaluation split across accounts to get additional free usage. Recommend we:
1) Deny cross-account stacked free credits (policy: no stacking across independent trial accounts).
2) Offer a single consolidated org-level pilot credit (200k tokens) tied to a short pilot agreement and single billing contact.
3) If Nimbus wants more, recommend converting to a paid pilot — offer 20% first-month credit on a pilot contract.

I’ve uploaded the IP evidence and signup fingerprints to the shared drive: https://drive.redwood.com/shared/nimbus-evidence/DB-83421 (see evidence_ips.txt). Happy to jump on a quick call if you want to walk through.

– Priyom
Fraud & Risk Analyst, Redwood Inference
priyom_das@redwood.com
Attachment: evidence_ips.txt
From: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.com>

Hi Alex —

Thanks for the details and the forecast. We completed a short compliance review and want to be transparent about our next steps.

Summary: our fraud team observed overlapping signup fingerprints and reuse of aliases that suggest the four trials were created in coordination rather than representing four unaffiliated customers. Our policy does not allow free credit stacking across independently created trial accounts.

What we can do right now:
- Approve a single consolidated org-level pilot credit of 200,000 tokens (valid for 6 weeks) if you provide a single billing contact and confirm legal entity (company registration link).
- If you need more capacity immediately, we can convert you to a paid pilot and provide a 20% first-month credit / discount.

Next steps (please reply with one):
1) Confirm which option you prefer and provide the single billing contact email and company filing link.
2) If you’d like the paid pilot option, I’ll have Ben share the simplified pilot SOW and pricing.

Apologies if this introduces friction — we aim to balance fair access with abuse prevention. If you’d like, we can set up a 20-minute call this week to finish details.

Best regards,
Mina Haddad
Senior Account Executive, Redwood Inference
